skill.name: git-workflow
skill.description: Guides Git work from conventional commit messages through branch naming, verification checks, commits, and push preparation.
skill.summary: Use a structured Git workflow for commits, branches, verification, and push readiness.
skill.author: Doyajin174

content.value_statement: Git work can drift into unclear commits and missed verification. This skill guides conventional commits, branch naming, checks, and push preparation.
actual_capabilities: Formats commit messages using conventional commit structure.
Suggests common commit types with examples.
Lists verification checks for tests, linting, type checks, and builds.
Provides branch naming patterns for features, fixes, and refactors.
Outlines staging, committing, verification, and push steps.
limitations: It does not inspect repository state unless the agent reads files or runs Git commands.
It does not replace project-specific release or review rules.
Example verification commands require matching package scripts in the project.
Commit and push steps can change local and remote repositories.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Work
use_cases.description: Create clear branch names, commit messages, and verification steps before opening review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Contributions
use_cases.description: Align contributors on conventional commits and shared completion checks.

use_cases.title: Verify Agent Changes
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist before an AI coding agent declares work complete.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users

prompt_templates.title: Create a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-workflow skill to write a conventional commit message for these changes: [summary].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-workflow skill to list the checks I should run before finishing this task.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-workflow skill to choose a branch name and commit sequence for this issue: [issue details].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-workflow skill to review my pending changes, propose commits, and identify verification gaps before push.

output_examples.input: I added login validation and updated tests.
output_examples.output: Suggested commit: feat(auth): add login validation. Run tests, linting, type checks, and the build before pushing.

output_examples.input: I need a branch for fixing issue 42 about null API responses.
output_examples.output: Suggested branch: fix/42-null-api-response. Use a fix commit type and verify the API tests before review.

output_examples.input: Check whether my task is ready to finish.
output: Confirm lint and type checks pass.

best_practices: Run project checks before committing or pushing changes.
Keep commit messages short, specific, and aligned with the actual change.
Confirm with the user before running commands that commit or push.
anti_patterns: Do not use a broad commit type when a precise type fits.
Do not declare work complete before verification commands finish.
Do not push changes before checking repository status and user intent.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. Any command execution depends on the agent environment and user approval rules.

faq.question: Which commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It uses conventional commit format with type, optional scope, description, body, and footer.

faq.question: Can it help choose a branch name?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives patterns for feature, fix, and refactor branches.

faq.question: What checks does it recommend before completion?
faq.answer: It recommends tests, linting, TypeScript checks when relevant, builds, committed changes, and removal of stray logging.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for AI coding assistants that support repository work.

faq.question: Does it replace team release rules?
faq.answer: No. Teams should apply their own review, release, and deployment requirements.
